content: Adapalene is a medication specifically prescribed for the treatment of acne. It belongs to a class of drugs known as retinoid-like compounds. Its mechanism of action involves preventing the formation of pimples beneath the skin's surface. Adapalene is available in several formulations, including a gel, a liquid solution, and a cream, all of which are applied topically to the skin. The solution is provided either in a glass bottle with an applicator or as single-use medicated wipes (pledgets). Typically, adapalene is applied once daily, preferably at bedtime. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label meticulously. If you have any uncertainties, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use adapalene exactly as prescribed; do not apply more or less of it, nor use it more frequently than directed. Increasing the amount or frequency of application will not accelerate or enhance the results but may lead to skin irritation. While adapalene helps manage acne, it does not cure it. During the initial weeks of treatment, your acne may appear to worsen, as the medication brings pre-existing pimples to the surface. It may take 8 to 12 weeks or longer to experience the full therapeutic benefits. Pimples typically take 6 to 8 weeks to form under the skin, so patience is necessary. Continue using adapalene even if your acne initially worsens or if you do not observe immediate improvement. Do not discontinue the medication without consulting your doctor. Avoid applying adapalene to areas of skin that are sunburned, broken, or affected by eczema. If you have any of these conditions, wait until your skin has healed before using the medication. Take care to prevent adapalene from coming into contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth. If accidental contact occurs, rinse the area thoroughly with water and contact your doctor, as irritation, swelling, or infection may result. To apply adapalene: 1. Gently cleanse the affected skin using a mild soap or soap-free cleanser, then pat it dry with a soft towel. Avoid harsh or abrasive cleansers and refrain from vigorous scrubbing. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for recommendations on gentle cleansers. 2. If using the gel or cream, apply a thin layer of the medication to the affected area using your fingers. For pledgets, remove one from its foil pouch and gently wipe the entire affected area. If using the solution in a glass bottle, use the provided applicator to apply a thin layer to the affected area. 3. You may experience a mild warmth or stinging sensation at the application site, which is normal and should subside shortly. 4. If using a pledget, discard it after use. Do not reuse it. Adapalene may also be prescribed for other medical purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before starting adapalene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to adapalene or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and skincare products you are using. Certain skincare products, particularly those that are harsh, drying, or contain alcohol, spices, lime rind, sulfur, resorcinol, salicylic acid, or alpha hydroxy acid, may irritate your skin when used with adapalene. If you have been using such products, your doctor may advise you to wait until your skin returns to normal before beginning adapalene treatment. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of eczema or cancer. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using adapalene, contact your doctor immediately. Adapalene may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight and extreme weather conditions, such as cold or wind. Avoid using hot wax for hair removal during treatment. There are no specific dietary restrictions while using adapalene unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Adapalene may cause side effects, particularly during the first 2 to 4 weeks of treatment. Common side effects include redness, scaling, dryness, burning or stinging, and itching. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. In laboratory studies, medications similar to adapalene have been associated with tumor development in animals exposed to sunlight or artificial UV light. It is unclear whether adapalene poses a similar risk to humans. Protect your skin from sunlight and sunlamps, and discuss potential risks with your doctor. If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store adapalene in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of accidental ingestion, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 immediately. Keep all medical appointments while using adapalene. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Adapalene is marketed under the brand name Differin®.
